propositions: The transition command has two distinct --force flags with conflicting meanings: a valueless --force that bypasses the start-work gate, and --force-close that bypasses the close gate, creating inconsistency with rebar claim's single --force[=reason] spelling

The rename collapses transition's two force flags into a single --force[=reason] that dispatches its behavior by target status: bypasses start-work gate on open->in_progress (with audit reason precedence: explicit value > --reason text > '(no reason given)'), and bypasses close gate on transitions to closed
Stale callers using --force-close must fail loudly with a CommandError naming --force rather than silently succeed, because the parser's hand-rolled token loop skips unknown tokens by default
The library kwarg rebar.transition(..., force_close=...) and internal Python identifiers retain their original names; only the CLI flag string is renamed

Concurrent change scripts/dependency_audit.py emitted the retired --force-close flag after the rename landed, causing runtime failures until fixed to use --force={reason}; a tree-wide guard test now re-validates any emitted argv against the live parser
